info.title: Tuteliq API
info.description:
# AI-Powered Child Safety API

You're building a chat feature for a kids' learning app. A user sends a message that looks innocuous on the surface but contains subtle grooming escalation patterns. Tuteliq catches it, scores the risk by the child's age group, and gives your trust & safety team an actionable report, typically in about a second, or around 400ms in fast mode on a dedicated deployment. One API call replaces months of in-house ML work.

---

## KOSA Harm Categories Coverage

| Harm Category | Endpoint | Status |
|--------------|----------|--------|
| Eating Disorders | `/safety/unsafe` | ✅ Covered |
| Substance Use | `/safety/unsafe` | ✅ Covered |
| Suicidal Behaviors | `/safety/unsafe` | ✅ Covered |
| Depression & Anxiety | `/safety/unsafe` + `/analysis/emotions` | ✅ Covered |
| Compulsive Usage | `/safety/unsafe` | ✅ Covered |
| Harassment & Bullying | `/safety/bullying` | ✅ Covered |
| Sexual Exploitation | `/safety/grooming` + `/safety/unsafe` | ✅ Covered |
| Voice & Audio Threats | `/safety/voice` | ✅ Covered |
| Visual Content Risks | `/safety/image` | ✅ Covered |

---

## Key Features

- **Age-Calibrated Severity** — Risk scores adjust across four age brackets (under 10, 10–12, 13–15, 16–17) so moderation matches developmental context.

- **Nuanced Context Recognition** — Distinguishes hyperbolic teen language from genuine crisis signals, dramatically reducing false positives.

- **Grooming Pattern Detection** — Identifies multi-stage grooming tactics: trust escalation, secrecy requests, isolation attempts, and boundary violations.

- **Emotional Trend Analysis** — Tracks persistent mood patterns across conversations to surface early indicators of declining mental health.

- **Voice & Image Analysis** — Upload audio or images for transcription, OCR, and full safety analysis in a single call.

- **Real-time Voice Streaming** — WebSocket endpoint for live audio moderation with configurable flush intervals and per-category alerts.

- **Guidance & Reports** — Generate age-appropriate action plans and professional incident reports ready for handoff to human reviewers.

- **Batch Processing & Webhooks** — Analyze up to 50 items per batch call, with HMAC-signed webhook alerts for critical incidents.

---

## Credits per Action

| Endpoint | Credits | Notes |
|----------|---------|-------|
| `detectBullying` | 1 | Single text analysis |
| `detectUnsafe` | 1 | Single text analysis |
| `detectGrooming` | 1 per 10 msgs | `ceil(messages / 10)`, min 1 |
| `analyzeEmotions` | 1 per 10 msgs | `ceil(messages / 10)`, min 1 |
| `getActionPlan` | 2 | Longer generation |
| `generateReport` | 3 | Structured output |
| `analyzeVoice` | 5 | Transcription + analysis |
| `analyzeImage` | 3 | Vision + OCR + analysis |

Every response includes a `credits_used` field. Credit balance is also available via the `X-Credits-Remaining` response header.

---

## Quick Start

**1.** Get your API key at [tuteliq.ai/dashboard](https://tuteliq.ai/dashboard)

**2.** Install the SDK:

```bash
npm install @tuteliq/sdk
```

**3.** Make your first call:

```typescript
import Tuteliq from '@tuteliq/sdk'

const tuteliq = new Tuteliq({ apiKey: 'YOUR_API_KEY' })

const result = await tuteliq.detectUnsafe({
  content: "Don't talk to your parents about us meeting up",
  context: { age_group: "13-15" }
})

console.log(result.unsafe)              // true
console.log(result.categories)          // ["grooming_adjacent", "secrecy"]
console.log(result.severity)            // "high"
console.log(result.recommended_action)  // "Escalate to moderator"
```

---

## Performance

| Metric | Value |
|--------|-------|
| Full detection, shared tier | ~1.4s typical |
| Fast mode (`verdict_only`), shared tier | ~1.0s typical |
| Fast mode, dedicated deployment | ~400ms |
| Uptime SLA | 99.9% |

Shared-tier figures are what a standard API key sees today. The dedicated figure is
the same model served on reserved hardware without the shared-tier hop, and is
available on enterprise plans rather than by default.

Check real-time status at [tuteliq.ai/status](https://tuteliq.ai/status)

adminSecret.name: x-admin-secret
adminSecret.description: Admin secret for privileged operational endpoints

get.description: Returns 200 if the service process is running. Use for Kubernetes liveness probe.
Returns 200 if the service is ready to accept traffic. Checks critical dependencies.
Returns detailed health status of all dependencies

mcp_version.description: Version of @tuteliq/mcp this image serves at /mcp

detector_version.description: Identifier of the deployed detection system. It changes whenever anything that can alter a verdict changes, so a result can be tied to the system that produced it.

detector_name.description: Name of the generation of the deployed detection system. It stays the same across the dated versions within a generation. Tie a result to `detector_version`, not to this.

build.description: The first seven characters of the commit the running image was built from. Present only when the deploy supplied one. The version above names a day; this tells two builds of the same day apart.

detector_config.description: A short fingerprint of the configuration the detection system is running with. It changes whenever that configuration changes, so two deployments of the same version can be told apart.

get.description: Returns detailed status of each dependency with configuration info. Requires admin authentication via X-Admin-Secret header or Authorization: Bearer token. Other health endpoints (/live, /ready, /health) remain public.

get.summary: Get API status and component health
get.description: Returns overall API status, component-level health (API, database, cache, AI engine), uptime percentages for the last 24h/7d/30d, and any active incidents. Use for status dashboards and monitoring.
Lightweight endpoint returning a minimal OK response. Designed for UptimeRobot, Pingdom, and similar monitoring services that just need a 200 response.

get.summary: List components available for granular pings
get.description: Returns the list of components exposed at `/status/ping/<component>`.

Returns 200 if the named component is healthy, 503 otherwise. Designed for UptimeRobot, Pingdom and similar. Probe results are cached for ~20 seconds to avoid hammering upstream services when multiple monitors poll.
Returns a self-contained HTML status page showing component health, uptime percentages, and incident history. Auto-refreshes every 60 seconds. Can be embedded in an iframe on your own status page.
Returns an HTML landing page for browsers or a JSON summary for API clients (curl, Postman). Includes links to documentation, dashboard, and current operational status.
Returns all active pricing plans. This endpoint is public and does not require authentication.
Returns detailed pricing plan information including limits and endpoints.

Points to the published Tuteliq legal documents and returns the two things a URL cannot convey to a machine: the retention schedule derived from the values the deletion job actually enforces, and each supported data subject right mapped to the live endpoint that exercises it. No authentication required — transparency by design.
Returns the current list of third-party sub-processors used by Tuteliq, including their purpose and data processing location. Required for GDPR Article 28 transparency. No authentication required.

Returns the data retention policy detailing how long each category of data is stored and when it is automatically purged. Covers detection results, audit logs, usage metrics, and account data. No authentication required.

get.summary: Get a signed liveness challenge nonce with randomized sequence
get.description: Returns a server-signed nonce and a randomized challenge sequence. The client must follow the prescribed order.

post.summary: Cloud IDS Pub/Sub push endpoint
post.description: Receives threat notifications from Google Cloud IDS via Pub/Sub push subscription. Verifies the token query parameter before processing.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: Pub/Sub verification token

post.summary: Bootstrap a wallet device via App Attest
post.description: Issues a short-lived JWT scoped to verify:submit. The iOS Tuteliq Wallet calls this once at first launch and re-uses the token until it nears expiry. Per-device rate limiting prevents bootstrap abuse.

get.description: Returns the current SDK-side prescreen lexicon: a set of high-precision phrase patterns mapped to category flags. SDKs run this client-side before calling detection endpoints — clearly-benign content can short-circuit the API call entirely, and positive signals can be attached to the request as structured hints. Public endpoint; lexicon is non-secret reference data.

version.description: Lexicon schema/content version. Bumped on any change. SDKs cache by this.

304.description: Lexicon unchanged since the If-None-Match etag you supplied.

delete.description: Permanently delete all stored account and analysis data associated with your API key. This is irreversible. All detection results, incidents, emotion records, and usage data will be purged. Returns confirmation and count of deleted records.

patch.description: Correct inaccurate personal data stored in your account. Specify the collection, document ID, and fields to update. Changes are audit-logged with the original and new values for compliance.

document_id.description: ID of the document to rectify

fields.description: Fields to update with corrected values

get.description: Download a complete JSON export of all data associated with your account: detection results, incidents, emotion analyses, consent records, and usage history. Returned as a downloadable JSON file for data portability.

post.summary: Record user consent
post.description: Record explicit consent for a specific processing purpose (e.g., data processing, marketing). Stores consent with timestamp, IP address, and user agent for audit compliance. Required before certain data processing activities under GDPR.

version.description: Version of the consent policy being accepted

get.description: Retrieve all active consent records for your account. Optionally filter by consent type. Returns consent type, version accepted, and timestamp for each record.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Filter by consent type

delete.summary: Withdraw consent for a processing purpose
delete.description: Withdraw previously given consent for a specific processing type. The withdrawal is recorded with timestamp for audit purposes. Any processing that relied on this consent will cease.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: The consent type to withdraw

get.description: Retrieve a chronological log of all data actions performed on your account: deletions, exports, consent changes, and rectifications. Supports filtering by action type and result limiting. Essential for demonstrating GDPR compliance.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: Filter by audit action type

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of entries to return

get.summary: Get API key count quota for current tier
get.description: Return the number of currently active API keys for the authenticated account, the per-tier maximum, and whether another key can be created. Dashboards must call this before minting a new key to enforce the plan limit.
List all MCP tokens associated with your account. These are scoped tokens issued to MCP clients like Claude Desktop.

delete.description: Revoke a specific MCP token. The MCP client using this token will be disconnected.

patch.description: Update the display name of an MCP token.

get.summary: Get the customer-registered public key for end-to-end incident encryption
get.description: Returns the public key currently used to encrypt incident records, or 404 if none is registered. When no key is registered, incidents fall back to server-side encryption (Tuteliq holds the key). Register a public key with POST to switch to true end-to-end encryption — only your dashboard can decrypt.

key_fingerprint.description: sha256(DER(SPKI)).hex — verify on your side to confirm integrity

post.summary: Register (or rotate) the public key Tuteliq uses to encrypt your incident records
post.description:
Registers an RSA public key. After registration, all NEW incident records (rationale, visual_description, etc.) are encrypted with a per-record AES key, which is itself wrapped with this RSA key (hybrid scheme RSA-OAEP + AES-256-GCM). Tuteliq cannot decrypt — only your dashboard (with the matching private key) can.

Rotating: POST a new key here. New incidents use the new key; old incidents remain readable with the old private key until they expire (90 days).

Private key is YOUR responsibility — Tuteliq cannot recover lost-key incidents.

algorithm.description: RSA-OAEP key size. 2048-bit is faster, 4096-bit is more conservative.

public_key_pem.description: PEM-encoded SPKI public key (begins with "-----BEGIN PUBLIC KEY-----").

delete.description: After revocation, new incidents fall back to server-side encryption (Tuteliq holds the key). Existing incidents stay encrypted under the previous key and remain readable only with its private key. Common reason to revoke: key compromise (then immediately register a new one).

get.summary: Get this account's Tuteliq Platform Safety Classification
get.description: Returns the saved daily snapshot of the account's operational safety classification, the same figure shown on the dashboard and the public Trust Center. It is computed once daily and read here as stored; this endpoint never recomputes or adjusts it, so all three surfaces always agree. `date` shows which day the snapshot is from. Returns 200 with `score: null` and `insufficient_data: true` when the account has too little activity to classify, and 404 when it has no classification at all. Neither is a zero score.

date.description: ISO date (UTC) the snapshot was computed. Always present, so a caller can see the figure is a daily snapshot rather than live.

score.description: 0-100. `null` when `insufficient_data` is true. Never treat null as zero.

insufficient_data.description: True when fewer than 5 real incidents have been processed. The account is not yet classified; it has not scored badly.

reason.description: Why the account is not yet classified.

tip.description: Improvement hint, present when the component is below full marks.

evidence.description: The inputs the score was computed from. Contains no personal data: no names, emails or message content.

incident_count.description: Real incidents counted. Test, sandbox and demo traffic is excluded by the job.

oldest_open_days.description: Age of the oldest `new` or `escalated` incident. 0 when the queue is empty.

applicable_modalities.description: Content types the platform offers. Scoring is measured only against these.

disclaimer.description: Carried in the payload deliberately. The dashboard card shows this next to the number; an API caller has no card, and a score published without it can be mistaken for a certification.

post.summary: Log a new data breach incident
post.description: Record a data breach for GDPR Article 33/34 compliance. Captures breach details, severity, affected users, and data categories involved. Automatically timestamps the report and initializes notification tracking. Use this as the first step in your breach response workflow.

data_categories.description: Categories of data affected (e.g., personal_data, analysis_results)

reported_by.description: Identifier of the person reporting the breach

get.description: Retrieve breach records with optional filtering by status (open, investigating, resolved, closed). Returns breach details, severity, affected user count, and current notification status. Use for breach dashboard and compliance reporting.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Filter by breach status

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of records to return

get.description: Retrieve full details of a specific breach incident including timeline, affected users, data categories, notification status, and any notes added during investigation.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Breach incident ID

patch.summary: Update breach status and notification progress
patch.description: Update a breach incident's status (investigating, resolved, closed) and notification progress. Add notes to document investigation findings or remediation steps. All updates are timestamped for the breach audit trail.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Breach incident ID

post.summary: Trigger manual data retention cleanup
post.description: Manually run the data retention cleanup process to purge records that have exceeded their retention period. Normally runs on a schedule, but can be triggered on-demand for compliance audits or storage management. Returns a summary of deleted records by category.

get.description: Retrieve stored IDS threat events with optional filtering by severity, date range, and limit.

parameters.name: severity
parameters.description: Filter by severity (e.g., CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW)

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: ISO date — only return threats since this date

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of records to return

get.description: Retrieve full details of a specific IDS threat event including raw log data.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Threat record ID

get.description: Returns summary counts of IDS threats by severity and time range.

post.summary: Validate and process a document image via session (mobile)
post.description: Per-step document validation for the cross-device flow. Checks image quality, then runs the document work (text extraction, face template) so that the submit step does not need the document image again: the session carries the result, never the image, until the session is submitted, cancelled, or expires. Send `side` (`front`, `back` or `passport`) and `document_type` as form fields ahead of the file. `retained: false` means the document was not held (encryption unavailable, or the document could not be processed) and must be included in the submit. Free, no credits consumed. Optional `capture_context` field (JSON): what captured the upload and which on-device checks ran, as the client reports it; malformed values are ignored, never rejected. Self-reported, so it can add warnings but never improve a result.

post.summary: Validate the data read from a document's NFC chip via session (mobile)
post.description: For apps that read the ICAO 9303 chip of a passport or ID card on the device. Upload the files exactly as read (`ef_com`, `dg1`, `ef_sod` required; `dg2`, `dg11`, `dg12`, `dg14`, `dg15` optional) with `document_type` as a form field. The server runs passive authentication over EF.SOD, cross-checks the chip MRZ against the photographed document, and, when valid, uses the chip MRZ and the chip portrait in place of the OCR'd MRZ and the photographed portrait. The photographed document is still required. Only the parsed MRZ and a face template are kept, until the session is submitted, cancelled, or expires; the chip files are not stored. `valid: false` means the chip data is not used and the verification relies on the photographed document. Free, no credits consumed. Optional `capture_context` field (JSON): what captured the upload and which on-device checks ran, as the client reports it; malformed values are ignored, never rejected. Self-reported, so it can add warnings but never improve a result.

usable_as_document.description: The chip read can stand in for the photographed document: the issuer is trusted, the chip portrait shows a face, and the chip proved it is the original, by signing this session's challenge (Active Authentication, `aa_signature`) or by answering under this session's Chip Authentication keys (`ca_response`). Under `chip_policy: instead_of_photo`, false means the session still needs a document photo.

get.summary: Get a challenge for the chip to sign (Active Authentication)
get.description: A fresh random challenge for this session. The app has the document chip sign it (ICAO 9303 Active Authentication) and uploads the signature as `aa_signature` with validate-chip, together with DG15. Single-use, valid for two minutes; asking again replaces it. A chip read can stand in for the document photo only with a valid signature over this challenge.

challenge.description: Hex-encoded random challenge (8 bytes, the length ICAO Doc 9303 defines). Send exactly these bytes to the chip.

post.summary: Start Chip Authentication (for chips without Active Authentication)
post.description: For chips that prove they are the original with ICAO 9303 Chip Authentication (DG14) rather than Active Authentication (DG15), as most recent European passports do. Send DG14 exactly as read, base64. The server agrees fresh session keys with the chip's key and returns the commands to send: `commands` in order under the chip session the app already has (each must answer 9000), then `protected_command` exactly as given, outside that session. Upload the chip's complete response to `protected_command` (data and status word) as `ca_response` with validate-chip, together with DG14. The server keeps only its own one-time private key, never anything from the chip; it is single-use and valid for two minutes, and starting again replaces it. Send `protected_command` last: the chip then uses the new keys, so read every file before.

dg14.description: DG14 exactly as read from the chip, base64.

commands.description: Hex APDUs to send in order under the current secure messaging.

protected_command.description: Hex APDU to send as is, after `commands`.

post.summary: Validate and assess a selfie via session (mobile)
post.description: Per-step selfie validation for the cross-device flow. Always checks that a face is present. When the request also carries the liveness capture (`liveness_frame` files and the `liveness_token` field), it runs the selfie assessment now (liveness, age estimation, and the face match against the document already processed by validate-document) and the session carries the DECISION, never the selfie or the frames, to submit, which then needs no images. `assessed: false` means the assessment did not run (no capture sent, or nothing to match against) and the submit must carry the selfie and liveness as before. Free, no credits consumed. Optional `capture_context` field (JSON): what captured the upload and which on-device checks ran, as the client reports it; malformed values are ignored, never rejected. Self-reported, so it can add warnings but never improve a result. Optional `liveness_frame_kinds` field (JSON array, one entry per `liveness_frame`: center, turn_left, turn_right, blink_closed, blink_open, smile, neutral).

reason.description: Why the selfie was refused, when it is something specific: `multiple_faces` means someone else is in the frame.

post.summary: Submit verification via session (mobile)
post.description: Complete a verification using a session token. When validate-document and validate-selfie already processed the document and the selfie for this session, this request needs no images at all and returns immediately. Otherwise send the selfie and liveness capture (and, unless validate-document processed them, the ID document images). Images included in this request always take precedence over what the session carries. Optional `capture_context` field (JSON): what captured the upload and which on-device checks ran, as the client reports it; malformed values are ignored, never rejected. Self-reported, so it can add warnings but never improve a result. Optional `liveness_frame_kinds` field (JSON array, one entry per `liveness_frame`: center, turn_left, turn_right, blink_closed, blink_open, smile, neutral). A submit is refused with VERIFY_11007 when the session has less than 6 minutes left of its 60-minute lifetime, so its verdict is always readable; create a new session in that case.

reason.description: With `status: document_required` from the chip policy: `chip_not_usable` (instead_of_photo, and the chip read cannot stand in: add a document photo) or `chip_required` (required, and no valid chip read yet).

post.summary: Report verification step progress from mobile
post.description: Used by mobile device to report which step the user is on, so desktop can show real-time progress.

get.summary: Which document sides the session already holds a processed result for
get.description: Session-token authenticated. Used by a device that resumed past the document steps while the other device was still reading the document: it polls this until the sides it needs are held, then continues without capturing the document again. Never returns document content.

get.summary: Resolve verification mode and language for end-user
get.description: Called by the HTML verification page on load. Detects the end-user country from IP, resolves the verification mode from market config, and returns the UI language. No authentication required — session ID is unguessable (128-bit entropy).

chip_policy.description: How a chip read counts as document evidence for this session, so the app shows the right steps.

auto_capture.description: Whether the page takes the document photo itself, as set when the session was created.

get.summary: Subscribe to session status updates via SSE
get.description: Server-Sent Events stream that emits status changes and results for a verification session. No authentication required — session ID is unguessable (128-bit entropy).

post.summary: Detect bullying, harassment, and intimidation in text
post.description: Analyze a message for bullying indicators including verbal abuse, social exclusion, threats, and cyberbullying patterns. Returns severity (low/medium/high/critical), bullying type classification, confidence score, and a recommended action. Risk scores are age-calibrated when context.ageGroup is provided.

role.description: Who this participant is, as your platform knows it.

age_group.description: This participant's age group, for example "8-10". For a child or teen it gives the child's age the detectors use.

sender.description: The sender, as your platform knows them. Declared, like an age: never inferred from the text.

role.description: Who this participant is, as your platform knows it.

age_group.description: This participant's age group, for example "8-10". For a child or teen it gives the child's age the detectors use.

relationship_to_sender.description: How this recipient is related to the sender. `guardian_of_sender` or `child_of_sender` applies the `family` setting; `educator_of_sender` or `student_of_sender` applies `education`.

recipients.description: The recipients and how each is related to the sender. A declared relationship supplies the setting, and a declared child or teen supplies the child's age, where the request did not send them; `participants_applied` in the response says what was applied. It never excuses harm: a declared guardian or educator doing harm is flagged like anyone else.

language.description: Language code (e.g., "en"). 33 supported languages: en is stable, the other 32 are beta (ar, bg, ca, cs, da, de, el, es, et, fi, fr, ga, hr, hu, it, ja, ko, lt, lv, mt, nl, no, pl, pt, ro, ru, sk, sl, sv, tr, uk, zh). The code is the documented form; the English name of a supported language is also accepted ("English" as "en"). A region or script suffix is read as its base language ("en-US" as "en"), and "nb" or "nn" as "no". A value that is not supported is refused with a 400 that lists the supported codes. Omit the field, or send "auto", and the language is detected from the text.

age_group.description: Alias for `ageGroup`, as the other detectors spell it. When both are given, `ageGroup` is used.

conversation_type.description: Optional, no default: omit it and behaviour is unchanged. The setting this conversation was captured in, declared by your platform from its own configuration, never from end-user input. A declared setting names the responsible party in the conversation: a counsellor or helpline worker (`helpline`, `clinical`), a clinician (`healthcare`), an officer or investigator (`law_enforcement`, `investigative`), an adviser taking a report (`fraud_report`, `abuse_report`, `support_disclosure`, `advisory`), a moderator (`moderation_review`), a lawyer, trainer, journalist or researcher (`legal`, `training`, `journalism`, `research`), a teacher, tutor or safeguarding lead (`education`), a parent or guardian (`family`). In any of these settings, a conversation in which a person is at risk, that responsible party is already handling it, and nothing is happening as the text is written, is kept visible at `monitor` without an alert, and `protective_speech_capped` says so. Harm being done in the conversation, by anyone including the responsible party, a person at risk with nobody acting, and anything acute alert as they would with no setting. On social engineering, app fraud, romance scam, mule recruitment, gambling harm and bullying, harm happening now to the writer, or to a specific other person the writer tells of, never ends below `flag_for_review` because of a setting, even with the responsible party handling it; `ongoing_harm_floor_applied` says when that held a result the setting would have lowered. Where the harm is discussed and not enacted (`fraud_report`, `abuse_report`, `support_disclosure`, `helpline`, `clinical`, `investigative`, `legal`, `advisory`, `training`, `journalism`, `research`, `moderation_review`) an urgent action is also capped to `flag_for_review`, and the response echoes `conversation_type_applied`. `direct_message`, `group_chat`, `public_post`, `customer_service` and `gaming_chat` change nothing. In `education` and `family` this applies only when the speaker is not the person at risk: a young person speaking for themselves to a teacher or a parent alerts as with no setting. Whenever a setting is in effect, from this field or from the account's `default_conversation_type`, the response names it in `conversation_type_in_effect` and says where it came from in `conversation_type_source`.

minor_disclosure_check.description: Optional, off unless true. For a platform that suspects users may get past its age verification. When true and the request declares an adult (an adult `age_group`, `child_age` of 18 or more, or `conversation_type` `dating`, `adult_community` or `workplace`), one extra narrow reading asks whether the speaker says they are under 18 in other words than a stated age (a school year, parental controls, a milestone), beside the analysis. On a yes the analysis runs without the declared age and adult audience, `declared_age_overridden` and `minor_disclosure` say so, and on `dating` or `adult_community` a result that asked for nothing is raised to `flag_for_review` (`minor_on_adult_platform_raised`). With it on, a plainly stated minor age ("im 15") is reported in `minor_disclosure` and raised on `dating` or `adult_community` the same way, with no extra call. Omitted or false: no extra call and behaviour is unchanged. A plainly stated minor age ("im 15") drops the declared adult age whatever this is set to, as it always has.

support_threshold.description: Minimum severity to show crisis support resources (default: high). Critical always shows.

verdict_only.description: Fast mode: skip generating `action_detail`, the moderator-guidance expansion of `recommended_action`. Lower latency and a smaller response; `rationale` (used for incident summaries) and the verdict itself (severity, categories, recommended_action, risk_score) are unchanged.

flag_profanity.description: Additive, deterministic word-list flag for plain profanity/vulgarity. Adds `profanity` to the response; never affects `is_bullying`, `severity`, `risk_score`, or `recommended_action`. Free — no extra credits. Not a harm classifier: does not cover slurs or hate speech, which the detector itself already handles with full context.

flag_risk_terms.description: Additive, deterministic word-list flag for bare drug and violence terms (e.g. "cocaine", "kill"). Adds `risk_terms` to the response; never affects `is_bullying`, `severity`, `risk_score`, or `recommended_action`. Free — no extra credits. Purely lexical: WILL fire on benign uses of an included term ("kill the lights") since it cannot read context the way the detector itself does — combine with the detector’s own verdict for a stricter policy, don’t use in isolation as a block decision.

support_threshold.description: Top-level alias for options.support_threshold. Minimum severity to show crisis support resources (default: high). Critical always shows.

continuation_token.description: Opaque signed token from a previous /bullying call. Carries derived analysis state — no message content is stored server-side.

reset_conversation.description: Discard any continuation_token and start a fresh conversation.

message_id.description: Optional customer-side message id for evidence pointers.

external_id.description: Your unique identifier (e.g. message ID, content ID) for correlating Tuteliq results with your own system. Echoed back in the response and included in webhook payloads so you can match alerts to the original content.

customer_id.description: Your end-customer identifier for multi-tenant / B2B2C scenarios. speaker_role.description: The speaker's relationship to the conduct described, so a report can be routed to a victim-protection queue rather than a sender-sanction one without parsing rationale prose. `enacting` = the speaker is bullying. `experiencing` = the speaker describes what was done to them. `reporting_other` = a bystander describing a third party's conduct, or relaying someone else's decision. `self_directed` = the speaker disparages only themselves. `unclear` = cannot be determined. Where the result asks for review and the role is `experiencing` or `reporting_other`, the message is reported bullying: `is_bullying` is false and `bullying_reported` is true. Presence, not authorship, with one exception: where the result asks for review (or more) and the speaker is the person being bullied or a bystander telling of it, this is `false` and `bullying_reported` is `true` (with `bullying_reported_by`), because the message reports bullying and does not do it; the action still asks for a person. post.summary: Detect grooming patterns in conversations
post.description: Analyze a sequence of messages for multi-stage grooming tactics: trust building, isolation, secrecy requests, boundary testing, and sexual escalation. Accepts full conversation history with sender roles to detect patterns that single-message analysis would miss. Returns grooming risk level, identified tactics as flags, and recommended intervention actions.

conversation_type.description: Optional, no default: omit it and behaviour is unchanged. The setting this conversation was captured in, declared by your platform from its own configuration, never from end-user input. A declared setting names the responsible party in the conversation: a counsellor or helpline worker (`helpline`, `clinical`), a clinician (`healthcare`), an officer or investigator (`law_enforcement`, `investigative`), an adviser taking a report (`fraud_report`, `abuse_report`, `support_disclosure`, `advisory`), a moderator (`moderation_review`), a lawyer, trainer, journalist or researcher (`legal`, `training`, `journalism`, `research`), a teacher, tutor or safeguarding lead (`education`), a parent or guardian (`family`). In any of these settings, a conversation in which a person is at risk, that responsible party is already handling it, and nothing is happening as the text is written, is kept visible at `monitor` without an alert, and `protective_speech_capped` says so. Harm being done in the conversation, by anyone including the responsible party, a person at risk with nobody acting, and anything acute alert as they would with no setting. On social engineering, app fraud, romance scam, mule recruitment, gambling harm and bullying, harm happening now to the writer, or to a specific other person the writer tells of, never ends below `flag_for_review` because of a setting, even with the responsible party handling it; `ongoing_harm_floor_applied` says when that held a result the setting would have lowered. Where the harm is discussed and not enacted (`fraud_report`, `abuse_report`, `support_disclosure`, `helpline`, `clinical`, `investigative`, `legal`, `advisory`, `training`, `journalism`, `research`, `moderation_review`) an urgent action is also capped to `flag_for_review`, and the response echoes `conversation_type_applied`. `direct_message`, `group_chat`, `public_post`, `customer_service` and `gaming_chat` change nothing. In `education` and `family` this applies only when the speaker is not the person at risk: a young person speaking for themselves to a teacher or a parent alerts as with no setting. Whenever a setting is in effect, from this field or from the account's `default_conversation_type`, the response names it in `conversation_type_in_effect` and says where it came from in `conversation_type_source`.

minor_disclosure_check.description: Optional, off unless true. For a platform that suspects users may get past its age verification. When true and the request declares an adult (an adult `age_group`, `child_age` of 18 or more, or `conversation_type` `dating`, `adult_community` or `workplace`), one extra narrow reading asks whether the speaker says they are under 18 in other words than a stated age (a school year, parental controls, a milestone), beside the analysis. On a yes the analysis runs without the declared age and adult audience, `declared_age_overridden` and `minor_disclosure` say so, and on `dating` or `adult_community` a result that asked for nothing is raised to `flag_for_review` (`minor_on_adult_platform_raised`). With it on, a plainly stated minor age ("im 15") is reported in `minor_disclosure` and raised on `dating` or `adult_community` the same way, with no extra call. Omitted or false: no extra call and behaviour is unchanged. A plainly stated minor age ("im 15") drops the declared adult age whatever this is set to, as it always has.

flags.description: Closed vocabulary of the grooming tactics and content categories found. Values outside this list are never returned. Tuteliq's published grooming taxonomy is eight per-message tactics: `flattery`, `photo_request`, `gift_giving`, `secrecy_request`, `meeting_request`, `isolation`, `boundary_pushing` and `reconnaissance`. `sexual_content`, `sexualization` and `sextortion` are content categories, not tactics. `grooming` is reserved and not currently returned.

relationship_frame.description: What the CONVERSATION CONTENT establishes about how the two participants know each other, reported factually so a finding can be routed. `established_offline` = they already knew each other in the physical world before this conversation (school, club, lesson, household, a stated and evidenced role). `online_only` = the contact exists only online or began online, INCLUDING a conversation working toward a first meeting. `unestablished` = the content settles neither. DESCRIPTIVE ONLY. This never changes `grooming_risk`, `risk_score`, `recommended_action` or `flags`, in the same way `speaker_role` is descriptive on /safety/bullying. DO NOT TREAT `established_offline` AS REASSURING, and do not build a rule that lowers risk because an adult is known to the child: most child sexual abuse is committed by someone the child already knows. Measured on the 270-conversation PAN12 problem-2 set, `online_only` was two and a half times MORE common in non-predatory conversations than predatory ones (0.517 vs 0.193), and `established_offline` was three times more common in predatory ones (0.173 vs 0.058). The stranger intuition runs backwards in real transcript data. Present only when at least one tactic was flagged, since it exists to route a finding. Absent if the classification fails.

disclosure_cleared.description: Adjustment the API applied to this result, reported for transparency. Descriptive only: route on `recommended_action`. Absent when it did not apply.

confidentiality_frame.description: The adult's own framing of who may know, described factually rather than judged. `unconditional_concealment` asks the child to keep something from someone with no stated limit; `limited_confidentiality` offers privacy but names a condition under which the adult would tell someone ("unless someone's at risk"), which is safeguarding practice rather than a secrecy demand; `guardian_included` tells the child to inform a parent or carer, or says the adult will.

flag_attribution.description: Which participant each flag is attributed to: tactic -> the `sender_role` values of the messages that carry it. Omitted when `speaker_stance` is `describing_third_party`, so a person reporting someone else's conduct is never named as its author. Attribution only; it does not change the verdict.

This endpoint never returns `block`: blocking the account alerts the suspected groomer, so an urgent case is `immediate_intervention` and `action_detail` says so. Human-readable guidance is in `action_detail`, not here.

post.summary: Detect KOSA-aligned harm signals in text
post.description: Comprehensive safety analysis covering all KOSA harm categories: self-harm and suicidal ideation, eating disorders, substance use, depression/anxiety indicators, compulsive usage patterns, sexual content, violence, and hate speech. Returns categorized findings with age-calibrated severity scoring. This is the recommended STARTING endpoint for broad content moderation, not a complete safety layer on its own. **Pair it with `/safety/bullying`, or call `/api/v1/analyse/multi`.** Peer-to-peer harassment, exposure or "fisha" accounts, and image-based abuse of a named person are scored by `/safety/bullying`; grooming trajectories by `/safety/grooming`; extremist recruitment by `/safety/radicalisation`. This endpoint also reports `unsafe: false` where the sender is DESCRIBING a harm rather than being subject to it (survivor testimony, news, a lesson, a child relaying something seen elsewhere), which is deliberate and keeps protective speech out of your queue, but means a message another detector would flag can come back clear here. Measured on our published kids-online-slang set, every case in that shape was caught by a sibling detector. If you call only this endpoint you inherit that boundary.

role.description: Who this participant is, as your platform knows it.

age_group.description: This participant's age group, for example "8-10". For a child or teen it gives the child's age the detectors use.

sender.description: The sender, as your platform knows them. Declared, like an age: never inferred from the text.

role.description: Who this participant is, as your platform knows it.

age_group.description: This participant's age group, for example "8-10". For a child or teen it gives the child's age the detectors use.

relationship_to_sender.description: How this recipient is related to the sender. `guardian_of_sender` or `child_of_sender` applies the `family` setting; `educator_of_sender` or `student_of_sender` applies `education`.

recipients.description: The recipients and how each is related to the sender. A declared relationship supplies the setting, and a declared child or teen supplies the child's age, where the request did not send them; `participants_applied` in the response says what was applied. It never excuses harm: a declared guardian or educator doing harm is flagged like anyone else.

age_group.description: Age group (e.g., "14-17")

language.description: Language code (e.g., "en"). 33 supported languages: en is stable, the other 32 are beta (ar, bg, ca, cs, da, de, el, es, et, fi, fr, ga, hr, hu, it, ja, ko, lt, lv, mt, nl, no, pl, pt, ro, ru, sk, sl, sv, tr, uk, zh). The code is the documented form; the English name of a supported language is also accepted ("English" as "en"). A region or script suffix is read as its base language ("en-US" as "en"), and "nb" or "nn" as "no". A value that is not supported is refused with a 400 that lists the supported codes. Omit the field, or send "auto", and the language is detected from the text.

role.description: Role of the sender (e.g., "user", "contact", "adult", "child")

prior_messages.description: Prior turns of this conversation, oldest first, submitted by you for this request only -- Tuteliq stores no message content, so nothing here is retained after the call completes. Use this when you already have the whole conversation in hand; use continuation_token instead when you are calling once per new message as it arrives.

conversation_type.description: Optional, no default: omit it and behaviour is unchanged. The setting this conversation was captured in, declared by your platform from its own configuration, never from end-user input. A declared setting names the responsible party in the conversation: a counsellor or helpline worker (`helpline`, `clinical`), a clinician (`healthcare`), an officer or investigator (`law_enforcement`, `investigative`), an adviser taking a report (`fraud_report`, `abuse_report`, `support_disclosure`, `advisory`), a moderator (`moderation_review`), a lawyer, trainer, journalist or researcher (`legal`, `training`, `journalism`, `research`), a teacher, tutor or safeguarding lead (`education`), a parent or guardian (`family`). In any of these settings, a conversation in which a person is at risk, that responsible party is already handling it, and nothing is happening as the text is written, is kept visible at `monitor` without an alert, and `protective_speech_capped` says so. Harm being done in the conversation, by anyone including the responsible party, a person at risk with nobody acting, and anything acute alert as they would with no setting. On social engineering, app fraud, romance scam, mule recruitment, gambling harm and bullying, harm happening now to the writer, or to a specific other person the writer tells of, never ends below `flag_for_review` because of a setting, even with the responsible party handling it; `ongoing_harm_floor_applied` says when that held a result the setting would have lowered. Where the harm is discussed and not enacted (`fraud_report`, `abuse_report`, `support_disclosure`, `helpline`, `clinical`, `investigative`, `legal`, `advisory`, `training`, `journalism`, `research`, `moderation_review`) an urgent action is also capped to `flag_for_review`, and the response echoes `conversation_type_applied`. `direct_message`, `group_chat`, `public_post`, `customer_service` and `gaming_chat` change nothing. In `education` and `family` this applies only when the speaker is not the person at risk: a young person speaking for themselves to a teacher or a parent alerts as with no setting. Whenever a setting is in effect, from this field or from the account's `default_conversation_type`, the response names it in `conversation_type_in_effect` and says where it came from in `conversation_type_source`.

minor_disclosure_check.description: Optional, off unless true. For a platform that suspects users may get past its age verification. When true and the request declares an adult (an adult `age_group`, `child_age` of 18 or more, or `conversation_type` `dating`, `adult_community` or `workplace`), one extra narrow reading asks whether the speaker says they are under 18 in other words than a stated age (a school year, parental controls, a milestone), beside the analysis. On a yes the analysis runs without the declared age and adult audience, `declared_age_overridden` and `minor_disclosure` say so, and on `dating` or `adult_community` a result that asked for nothing is raised to `flag_for_review` (`minor_on_adult_platform_raised`). With it on, a plainly stated minor age ("im 15") is reported in `minor_disclosure` and raised on `dating` or `adult_community` the same way, with no extra call. Omitted or false: no extra call and behaviour is unchanged. A plainly stated minor age ("im 15") drops the declared adult age whatever this is set to, as it always has.

support_threshold.description: Minimum severity to show crisis support resources (default: high). Critical always shows.

verdict_only.description: Fast mode: skip generating `action_detail`, the moderator-guidance expansion of `recommended_action`. Lower latency and a smaller response; `rationale` (used for incident summaries) and the verdict itself (severity, categories, recommended_action, risk_score) are unchanged.

flag_profanity.description: Additive, deterministic word-list flag for plain profanity/vulgarity. Adds `profanity` to the response; never affects `unsafe`, `severity`, `risk_score`, or `recommended_action`. Free — no extra credits. Not a harm classifier: does not cover slurs or hate speech, which the detector itself already handles with full context.

flag_risk_terms.description: Additive, deterministic word-list flag for bare drug and violence terms (e.g. "cocaine", "kill"). Adds `risk_terms` to the response; never affects `unsafe`, `severity`, `risk_score`, or `recommended_action`. Free — no extra credits. Purely lexical: WILL fire on benign uses of an included term ("kill the lights") since it cannot read context the way the detector itself does — combine with the detector’s own verdict for a stricter policy, don’t use in isolation as a block decision.

support_threshold.description: Top-level alias for options.support_threshold. Minimum severity to show crisis support resources (default: high). Critical always shows.

continuation_token.description: Opaque signed token from a previous /unsafe call. Carries derived analysis state — no message content is stored server-side.

reset_conversation.description: Discard any continuation_token and start a fresh conversation.

new_conversation.description: Cross into a new conversation WITHOUT discarding the sustained_hopelessness pattern carried in continuation_token — unlike reset_conversation, which discards everything. Requires continuation_token to also be set. Use this when a new conversation starts on your side (e.g. a new chat session days later) but you still want Tuteliq to notice if the same pattern keeps recurring across those sessions.

message_id.description: Optional customer-side message id for evidence pointers.

external_id.description: Your unique identifier (e.g. message ID, content ID) for correlating Tuteliq results with your own system. Echoed back in the response and included in webhook payloads so you can match alerts to the original content.

customer_id.description: Your end-customer identifier for multi-tenant / B2B2C scenarios. If you serve multiple customers (schools, apps, brands) from a single API key, set this to route webhook alerts to the correct customer. Echoed back in the response and included in webhook payloads as "customerId".

metadata.description: Arbitrary key-value pairs for additional context (e.g. { "channel": "discord", "region": "eu" }). Stored with the detection result, echoed in the response, and included in webhook payloads. Maximum 20 properties.

incident_moderation_enabled.description: Per-call override of your account incident logging setting. When set, it takes precedence over the account-level flag for THIS request: true forces the incident to be persisted, false suppresses persistence. Omit to use your account default (which itself defaults to enabled). Lets you control incident logging per request, e.g. suppress logging for test traffic.

Returned as `attestation`; when none can be produced it is null and `attestation_reason` says why. It proves what was detected, not that the detection is correct. Sandbox keys are never signed.

urgency_kept_reason.description: Human-readable explanation. Present only when urgency_kept is true.

conversation_type_in_effect.description: The declared setting in effect for this request, from `context.conversation_type` or, when the request sent none, from your account's `default_conversation_type`. Present whenever a setting was in effect, whether or not it changed the result; absent when none was. Unlike `conversation_type_applied`, which is present only when the setting changed routing.

conversation_type_source.description: Where `conversation_type_in_effect` came from: `request` (sent with this request), `participants` (the relationship declared in `context.recipients`) or `account_default` (your account's `default_conversation_type`). Present only with `conversation_type_in_effect`.

participants_applied.description: What the declared `context.sender` and `context.recipients` supplied to this request: the setting their relationship names, and a declared child's age group and age. Present only when something was applied.

conversation_type_applied.description: Present only when a caller-declared `context.conversation_type` actually changed routing. Confirms the setting was taken into account, rather than leaving the platform to assume it was.

unsafe.description: Unsafe-content signal observed at ANY severity (including low / monitor cases). For production branching prefer `recommended_action` (`flag_for_review` / `block` / `immediate_intervention`), which is a stable enum, over the bare presence of a signal. SCOPED TO THIS ENDPOINT: `false` means no KOSA-category signal was found HERE, not that the content is safe. It is also `false` where the sender is describing a harm rather than being subject to it. Peer harassment and image-based abuse of a named person are scored by `/safety/bullying`, so do not read `false` as a clearance without also calling that endpoint or `/api/v1/analyse/multi`.

DESCRIPTIVE: the statement is still scored as if genuine, because presenting a disclosure as a test is also how a real one gets minimised, so this marks the frame for a reviewer rather than discounting it. Absent when nothing applies. ADVISORY: for a moderator UI and triage queues. Do not branch production logic on it; use `recommended_action`, which is a stable enum.

recipients.description: The recipients and how each is related to the sender. A declared relationship supplies the setting, and a declared child or teen supplies the child's age, where the request did not send them; `participants_applied` in the response says what was applied. It never excuses harm: a declared guardian or educator doing harm is flagged like anyone else.

language.description: Language code (e.g., "en"). 33 supported languages: en is stable, the other 32 are beta (ar, bg, ca, cs, da, de, el, es, et, fi, fr, ga, hr, hu, it, ja, ko, lt, lv, mt, nl, no, pl, pt, ro, ru, sk, sl, sv, tr, uk, zh). The code is the documented form; the English name of a supported language is also accepted ("English" as "en"). A region or script suffix is read as its base language ("en-US" as "en"), and "nb" or "nn" as "no". A value that is not supported is refused with a 400 that lists the supported codes. Omit the field, or send "auto", and the language is detected from the text.

conversation_type.description: Optional, no default: omit it and behaviour is unchanged. The setting this conversation was captured in, declared by your platform from its own configuration, never from end-user input. A declared setting names the responsible party in the conversation: a counsellor or helpline worker (`helpline`, `clinical`), a clinician (`healthcare`), an officer or investigator (`law_enforcement`, `investigative`), an adviser taking a report (`fraud_report`, `abuse_report`, `support_disclosure`, `advisory`), a moderator (`moderation_review`), a lawyer, trainer, journalist or researcher (`legal`, `training`, `journalism`, `research`), a teacher, tutor or safeguarding lead (`education`), a parent or guardian (`family`). In any of these settings, a conversation in which a person is at risk, that responsible party is already handling it, and nothing is happening as the text is written, is kept visible at `monitor` without an alert, and `protective_speech_capped` says so. Harm being done in the conversation, by anyone including the responsible party, a person at risk with nobody acting, and anything acute alert as they would with no setting. On social engineering, app fraud, romance scam, mule recruitment, gambling harm and bullying, harm happening now to the writer, or to a specific other person the writer tells of, never ends below `flag_for_review` because of a setting, even with the responsible party handling it; `ongoing_harm_floor_applied` says when that held a result the setting would have lowered. Where the harm is discussed and not enacted (`fraud_report`, `abuse_report`, `support_disclosure`, `helpline`, `clinical`, `investigative`, `legal`, `advisory`, `training`, `journalism`, `research`, `moderation_review`) an urgent action is also capped to `flag_for_review`, and the response echoes `conversation_type_applied`. `direct_message`, `group_chat`, `public_post`, `customer_service` and `gaming_chat` change nothing. In `education` and `family` this applies only when the speaker is not the person at risk: a young person speaking for themselves to a teacher or a parent alerts as with no setting. Whenever a setting is in effect, from this field or from the account's `default_conversation_type`, the response names it in `conversation_type_in_effect` and says where it came from in `conversation_type_source`.

minor_disclosure_check.description: Optional, off unless true. For a platform that suspects users may get past its age verification. When true and the request declares an adult (an adult `age_group`, `child_age` of 18 or more, or `conversation_type` `dating`, `adult_community` or `workplace`), one extra narrow reading asks whether the speaker says they are under 18 in other words than a stated age (a school year, parental controls, a milestone), beside the analysis. On a yes the analysis runs without the declared age and adult audience, `declared_age_overridden` and `minor_disclosure` say so, and on `dating` or `adult_community` a result that asked for nothing is raised to `flag_for_review` (`minor_on_adult_platform_raised`). With it on, a plainly stated minor age ("im 15") is reported in `minor_disclosure` and raised on `dating` or `adult_community` the same way, with no extra call. Omitted or false: no extra call and behaviour is unchanged. A plainly stated minor age ("im 15") drops the declared adult age whatever this is set to, as it always has.

conversation_type.description: Optional, no default: omit it and behaviour is unchanged. The setting this conversation was captured in, declared by your platform from its own configuration, never from end-user input. A declared setting names the responsible party in the conversation: a counsellor or helpline worker (`helpline`, `clinical`), a clinician (`healthcare`), an officer or investigator (`law_enforcement`, `investigative`), an adviser taking a report (`fraud_report`, `abuse_report`, `support_disclosure`, `advisory`), a moderator (`moderation_review`), a lawyer, trainer, journalist or researcher (`legal`, `training`, `journalism`, `research`), a teacher, tutor or safeguarding lead (`education`), a parent or guardian (`family`). In any of these settings, a conversation in which a person is at risk, that responsible party is already handling it, and nothing is happening as the text is written, is kept visible at `monitor` without an alert, and `protective_speech_capped` says so. Harm being done in the conversation, by anyone including the responsible party, a person at risk with nobody acting, and anything acute alert as they would with no setting. On social engineering, app fraud, romance scam, mule recruitment, gambling harm and bullying, harm happening now to the writer, or to a specific other person the writer tells of, never ends below `flag_for_review` because of a setting, even with the responsible party handling it; `ongoing_harm_floor_applied` says when that held a result the setting would have lowered. Where the harm is discussed and not enacted (`fraud_report`, `abuse_report`, `support_disclosure`, `helpline`, `clinical`, `investigative`, `legal`, `advisory`, `training`, `journalism`, `research`, `moderation_review`) an urgent action is also capped to `flag_for_review`, and the response echoes `conversation_type_applied`. `direct_message`, `group_chat`, `public_post`, `customer_service` and `gaming_chat` change nothing. In `education` and `family` this applies only when the speaker is not the person at risk: a young person speaking for themselves to a teacher or a parent alerts as with no setting. Whenever a setting is in effect, from this field or from the account's `default_conversation_type`, the response names it in `conversation_type_in_effect` and says where it came from in `conversation_type_source`.

minor_disclosure_check.description: Optional, off unless true. For a platform that suspects users may get past its age verification. When true and the request declares an adult (an adult `age_group`, `child_age` of 18 or more, or `conversation_type` `dating`, `adult_community` or `workplace`), one extra narrow reading asks whether the speaker says they are under 18 in other words than a stated age (a school year, parental controls, a milestone), beside the analysis. On a yes the analysis runs without the declared age and adult audience, `declared_age_overridden` and `minor_disclosure` say so, and on `dating` or `adult_community` a result that asked for nothing is raised to `flag_for_review` (`minor_on_adult_platform_raised`). With it on, a plainly stated minor age ("im 15") is reported in `minor_disclosure` and raised on `dating` or `adult_community` the same way, with no extra call. Omitted or false: no extra call and behaviour is unchanged. A plainly stated minor age ("im 15") drops the declared adult age whatever this is set to, as it always has.

minor_disclosure.description: Present when the request declared an adult and the speaker says they are under 18, by stating an age or in other words. The declared adult age or setting was then not used, and `declared_age_overridden` says so. Never set by a stated adult age. Absent otherwise.

conversation_type.description: Optional, no default: omit it and behaviour is unchanged. The setting this conversation was captured in, declared by your platform from its own configuration, never from end-user input. A declared setting names the responsible party in the conversation: a counsellor or helpline worker (`helpline`, `clinical`), a clinician (`healthcare`), an officer or investigator (`law_enforcement`, `investigative`), an adviser taking a report (`fraud_report`, `abuse_report`, `support_disclosure`, `advisory`), a moderator (`moderation_review`), a lawyer, trainer, journalist or researcher (`legal`, `training`, `journalism`, `research`), a teacher, tutor or safeguarding lead (`education`), a parent or guardian (`family`). In any of these settings, a conversation in which a person is at risk, that responsible party is already handling it, and nothing is happening as the text is written, is kept visible at `monitor` without an alert, and `protective_speech_capped` says so. Harm being done in the conversation, by anyone including the responsible party, a person at risk with nobody acting, and anything acute alert as they would with no setting. On social engineering, app fraud, romance scam, mule recruitment, gambling harm and bullying, harm happening now to the writer, or to a specific other person the writer tells of, never ends below `flag_for_review` because of a setting, even with the responsible party handling it; `ongoing_harm_floor_applied` says when that held a result the setting would have lowered. Where the harm is discussed and not enacted (`fraud_report`, `abuse_report`, `support_disclosure`, `helpline`, `clinical`, `investigative`, `legal`, `advisory`, `training`, `journalism`, `research`, `moderation_review`) an urgent action is also capped to `flag_for_review`, and the response echoes `conversation_type_applied`. `direct_message`, `group_chat`, `public_post`, `customer_service` and `gaming_chat` change nothing. In `education` and `family` this applies only when the speaker is not the person at risk: a young person speaking for themselves to a teacher or a parent alerts as with no setting. Whenever a setting is in effect, from this field or from the account's `default_conversation_type`, the response names it in `conversation_type_in_effect` and says where it came from in `conversation_type_source`.

conversation_type.description: Optional, no default: omit it and behaviour is unchanged. The setting this conversation was captured in, declared by your platform from its own configuration, never from end-user input. A declared setting names the responsible party in the conversation: a counsellor or helpline worker (`helpline`, `clinical`), a clinician (`healthcare`), an officer or investigator (`law_enforcement`, `investigative`), an adviser taking a report (`fraud_report`, `abuse_report`, `support_disclosure`, `advisory`), a moderator (`moderation_review`), a lawyer, trainer, journalist or researcher (`legal`, `training`, `journalism`, `research`), a teacher, tutor or safeguarding lead (`education`), a parent or guardian (`family`). In any of these settings, a conversation in which a person is at risk, that responsible party is already handling it, and nothing is happening as the text is written, is kept visible at `monitor` without an alert, and `protective_speech_capped` says so. Harm being done in the conversation, by anyone including the responsible party, a person at risk with nobody acting, and anything acute alert as they would with no setting. On social engineering, app fraud, romance scam, mule recruitment, gambling harm and bullying, harm happening now to the writer, or to a specific other person the writer tells of, never ends below `flag_for_review` because of a setting, even with the responsible party handling it; `ongoing_harm_floor_applied` says when that held a result the setting would have lowered. Where the harm is discussed and not enacted (`fraud_report`, `abuse_report`, `support_disclosure`, `helpline`, `clinical`, `investigative`, `legal`, `advisory`, `training`, `journalism`, `research`, `moderation_review`) an urgent action is also capped to `flag_for_review`, and the response echoes `conversation_type_applied`. `direct_message`, `group_chat`, `public_post`, `customer_service` and `gaming_chat` change nothing. In `education` and `family` this applies only when the speaker is not the person at risk: a young person speaking for themselves to a teacher or a parent alerts as with no setting. Whenever a setting is in effect, from this field or from the account's `default_conversation_type`, the response names it in `conversation_type_in_effect` and says where it came from in `conversation_type_source`.

minor_disclosure_check.description: Optional, off unless true. For a platform that suspects users may get past its age verification. When true and the request declares an adult (an adult `age_group`, `child_age` of 18 or more, or `conversation_type` `dating`, `adult_community` or `workplace`), one extra narrow reading asks whether the speaker says they are under 18 in other words than a stated age (a school year, parental controls, a milestone), beside the analysis. On a yes the analysis runs without the declared age and adult audience, `declared_age_overridden` and `minor_disclosure` say so, and on `dating` or `adult_community` a result that asked for nothing is raised to `flag_for_review` (`minor_on_adult_platform_raised`). With it on, a plainly stated minor age ("im 15") is reported in `minor_disclosure` and raised on `dating` or `adult_community` the same way, with no extra call. Omitted or false: no extra call and behaviour is unchanged. A plainly stated minor age ("im 15") drops the declared adult age whatever this is set to, as it always has.

conversation_type.description: Optional, no default: omit it and behaviour is unchanged. In any of these settings, a conversation in which a person is at risk, that responsible party is already handling it, and nothing is happening as the text is written, is kept visible at `monitor` without an alert, and `protective_speech_capped` says so. Harm being done in the conversation, by anyone including the responsible party, a person at risk with nobody acting, and anything acute alert as they would with no setting. On social engineering, app fraud, romance scam, mule recruitment, gambling harm and bullying, harm happening now to the writer, or to a specific other person the writer tells of, never ends below `flag_for_review` because of a setting, even with the responsible party handling it; `ongoing_harm_floor_applied` says when that held a result the setting would have lowered. conversation_type.description: Optional, no default: omit it and behaviour is unchanged. The setting this conversation was captured in, declared by your platform from its own configuration, never from end-user input. A declared setting names the responsible party in the conversation: a counsellor or helpline worker (`helpline`, `clinical`), a clinician (`healthcare`), an officer or investigator (`law_enforcement`, `investigative`), an adviser taking a report (`fraud_report`, `abuse_report`, `support_disclosure`, `advisory`), a moderator (`moderation_review`), a lawyer, trainer, journalist or researcher (`legal`, `training`, `journalism`, `research`), a teacher, tutor or safeguarding lead (`education`), a parent or guardian (`family`). In any of these settings, a conversation in which a person is at risk, that responsible party is already handling it, and nothing is happening as the text is written, is kept visible at `monitor` without an alert, and `protective_speech_capped` says so. Harm being done in the conversation, by anyone including the responsible party, a person at risk with nobody acting, and anything acute alert as they would with no setting. On social engineering, app fraud, romance scam, mule recruitment, gambling harm and bullying, harm happening now to the writer, or to a specific other person the writer tells of, never ends below `flag_for_review` because of a setting, even with the responsible party handling it; `ongoing_harm_floor_applied` says when that held a result the setting would have lowered. Where the harm is discussed and not enacted (`fraud_report`, `abuse_report`, `support_disclosure`, `helpline`, `clinical`, `investigative`, `legal`, `advisory`, `training`, `journalism`, `research`, `moderation_review`) an urgent action is also capped to `flag_for_review`, and the response echoes `conversation_type_applied`. `direct_message`, `group_chat`, `public_post`, `customer_service` and `gaming_chat` change nothing. In `education` and `family` this applies only when the speaker is not the person at risk: a young person speaking for themselves to a teacher or a parent alerts as with no setting. Whenever a setting is in effect, from this field or from the account's `default_conversation_type`, the response names it in `conversation_type_in_effect` and says where it came from in `conversation_type_source`.

minor_disclosure_check.description: Optional, off unless true. For a platform that suspects users may get past its age verification. When true and the request declares an adult (an adult `age_group`, `child_age` of 18 or more, or `conversation_type` `dating`, `adult_community` or `workplace`), one extra narrow reading asks whether the speaker says they are under 18 in other words than a stated age (a school year, parental controls, a milestone), beside the analysis. On a yes the analysis runs without the declared age and adult audience, `declared_age_overridden` and `minor_disclosure` say so, and on `dating` or `adult_community` a result that asked for nothing is raised to `flag_for_review` (`minor_on_adult_platform_raised`). With it on, a plainly stated minor age ("im 15") is reported in `minor_disclosure` and raised on `dating` or `adult_community` the same way, with no extra call. Omitted or false: no extra call and behaviour is unchanged. A plainly stated minor age ("im 15") drops the declared adult age whatever this is set to, as it always has.

post.summary: Detect linguistic distress-signal patterns (pre-vulnerability indicators)
post.description: Analyses text for the presence of linguistic patterns historically associated with distress (loneliness expressions, isolation language, hopelessness phrases, trust-seeking openers, withdrawal references, family-conflict mentions). Returns pattern detections and, where applicable, downstream exploitation-risk assessment (grooming, sextortion, trafficking, radicalisation). Does NOT infer the author’s inner emotional state. Intended for child-safety contexts as a safety component (EU AI Act Art 5(1)(f) safety exception); not intended for workplace or general education monitoring.

endpoint.description: The detection endpoint that produced this result

detected.description: A signal was observed at ANY severity (including low / monitor cases). For production branching prefer `recommended_action` (`flag_for_moderator` / `immediate_intervention` indicate action required).

risk_score.description: Age-adjusted risk score (0.0-1.0)

tactic.description: The tactic or indicator this evidence relates to

recommended_action.description: Routing key, weakest to strongest: `none`, `monitor`, `flag_for_review`, `block`, `immediate_intervention`. Take automated action at `flag_for_review` and above. `monitor` means keep it visible and do nothing yet; it is common on ordinary conversations on the fraud and coercion routes, so acting on anything other than `none` acts on many harmless ones.

language.description: Language code used for analysis

continuation_token.description: Opaque, signed token carrying derived analysis state. Pass it back on the next call to continue the conversation without re-sending history. Server stores nothing — the token IS the state.

continuation_expires_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp at which the continuation_token expires (24h default).

state_source.description: How the prior analysis state was sourced for this call: "token" (decoded from continuation_token), "fresh" (no prior state), "reset" (reset_conversation forced a fresh start).
