speaker_role.description: The speaker's relationship to the conduct described, derived from the content by a separate classifier so it cannot move the verdict. `enacting` = the speaker is carrying the abuse out. `experiencing` = the abuse is directed at them, which is what a victim disclosure looks like. `reporting_other` = a bystander, support worker or professional describing someone else's conduct. `self_directed` = the speaker refers only to themselves. `unclear` = cannot be determined. This is the ONLY field that separates a victim from a perpetrator on this endpoint: `detected`, `severity` and `recommended_action` are the same for both, because the abuse being described is equally real either way. Read it before you action the sender, or you will sanction the person who reported the abuse. DESCRIPTIVE ONLY: it never changes `detected`, `severity`, `risk_score` or `recommended_action`, and it is derived independently of the caller-declared `conversation_type`. Same vocabulary as `speaker_role` on /safety/bullying.

attestation.description: Present only when the request set `attestation: true`. Null when none could be produced; see `attestation_reason`.

harm_descriptor.description: What was detected, non-identifying by construction.

external_ref.description: Your external_id, echoed verbatim. Not covered by the signature, and never stored by Tuteliq.

disclosure_url.description: Where this detector's published performance, including known weaknesses, is.

limits.description: What the attestation does not prove, carried inside it.

attestation_reason.description: Present only when an attestation was asked for and `attestation` is null: `nothing_detected`, `endpoint_unsupported`, `not_attributable` (the detector reads the speaker as the person it is happening to, a reporter or speaking of themselves: `speaker_role` experiencing, reporting_other or self_directed, or `speaker_stance` describing_third_party; always on social-engineering, app-fraud, gambling-harm, unsafe and distress-signals, which do not say who is speaking), `signing_unavailable` (signing or storage failed; the detection is unaffected) or `sandbox`.

post.summary: Read a display name and return a signal
post.description: Reads a nickname, handle or clan tag part by part, in its language and setting, and returns a signal, the categories it fell in, a reason a moderator can act on, and a recommendation: `allow`, `allow_and_watch`, `ask_to_rename` or `hold_for_review`. A name is judged by what it says, not by a word list: the same letters can be a surname, a year, a place or a team. A name the reading cannot place returns `none`. If the reading does not finish the answer is `none` with `reading_complete: false`, and it is not charged. Nothing is stored.

name.description: The display name, as the player typed it.

strictness.description: How readily a doubtful reading is acted on. A clear concern is acted on at every level. Default `balanced`.

language.description: Language of the name, as a two-letter code.

age_group.description: Age or age group of the account holder.

conversation_type.description: The setting the name is shown in, for example `gaming_chat`.

platform_reserved.description: Names the platform itself uses for staff or support, so a copy of one can be told from the real thing.

signal.description: A signal about the name, not a verdict on the person.

categories.description: From a closed list. Empty unless the signal is `review`.

text.description: The part of the name, as it appears in it.

parts.description: How each part of the name was read.

rationale.description: Why, in plain words a moderator can act on. No slurs are reproduced.

recommendation.description: Advice to the platform, which decides. Never an emergency action: a name alone cannot carry that.

recommendation_detail.description: One sentence on what the recommendation means.

confidence.description: 0 to 1. 0 when the reading did not complete.

reading_complete.description: False when the reading did not finish. Then `signal` is `none` because nothing was analysed, not because nothing was found; retry.

credits_used.description: 1 for a reading, 0 when the reading did not complete.

post.summary: Remove personal data from a text or a conversation

text.description: One text to redact. Send this or `messages`.

messages.description: The messages of one conversation, in order; the same value gets the same placeholder in every message.

language.description: Two-letter language code, when known.

mode.description: `protective` (default) also removes numbers shaped like a card, IBAN or ID number whose check digit fails, such as a mistyped real one. `precise` removes those only when the check digit passes. Every other type is removed in both modes.

strict_anonymisation.description: Off unless true. Also removes age, school year, supervision, gender, nationality or ethnicity, everyday places and health (English patterns). Safety review reads these, so use it only for text shared after analysis.

model_applied.description: Adjustment the API applied to this result, reported for transparency. Descriptive only: route on `recommended_action`. Absent when it did not apply.

post.summary: Fan-out analysis across multiple detection endpoints
post.description: Submit text to multiple detection endpoints in a single request. All endpoints run in parallel via Promise.allSettled. If vulnerability-exploitation is included and succeeds, its cross_endpoint_modifier is applied to all other results' severity scores (clamped to 1.0). Maximum 10 endpoints per request.

endpoints.description: List of endpoint names to run analysis against

role.description: Who this participant is, as your platform knows it.

age_group.description: This participant's age group, for example "8-10". For a child or teen it gives the child's age the detectors use.

sender.description: The sender, as your platform knows them. Declared, like an age: never inferred from the text.

role.description: Who this participant is, as your platform knows it.

age_group.description: This participant's age group, for example "8-10". For a child or teen it gives the child's age the detectors use.

relationship_to_sender.description: How this recipient is related to the sender. `guardian_of_sender` or `child_of_sender` applies the `family` setting; `educator_of_sender` or `student_of_sender` applies `education`.

recipients.description: The recipients and how each is related to the sender. A declared relationship supplies the setting, and a declared child or teen supplies the child's age, where the request did not send them; `participants_applied` in the response says what was applied. It never excuses harm: a declared guardian or educator doing harm is flagged like anyone else.

language.description: Language code (e.g., "en"). 33 supported languages: en is stable, the other 32 are beta (ar, bg, ca, cs, da, de, el, es, et, fi, fr, ga, hr, hu, it, ja, ko, lt, lv, mt, nl, no, pl, pt, ro, ru, sk, sl, sv, tr, uk, zh). The code is the documented form; the English name of a supported language is also accepted ("English" as "en"). A region or script suffix is read as its base language ("en-US" as "en"), and "nb" or "nn" as "no". A value that is not supported is refused with a 400 that lists the supported codes. Omit the field, or send "auto", and the language is detected from the text.

conversation_type.description: Optional, no default: omit it and behaviour is unchanged. The setting this conversation was captured in, declared by your platform from its own configuration, never from end-user input. A declared setting names the responsible party in the conversation: a counsellor or helpline worker (`helpline`, `clinical`), a clinician (`healthcare`), an officer or investigator (`law_enforcement`, `investigative`), an adviser taking a report (`fraud_report`, `abuse_report`, `support_disclosure`, `advisory`), a moderator (`moderation_review`), a lawyer, trainer, journalist or researcher (`legal`, `training`, `journalism`, `research`), a teacher, tutor or safeguarding lead (`education`), a parent or guardian (`family`). In any of these settings, a conversation in which a person is at risk, that responsible party is already handling it, and nothing is happening as the text is written, is kept visible at `monitor` without an alert, and `protective_speech_capped` says so. Harm being done in the conversation, by anyone including the responsible party, a person at risk with nobody acting, and anything acute alert as they would with no setting. On social engineering, app fraud, romance scam, mule recruitment, gambling harm and bullying, harm happening now to the writer, or to a specific other person the writer tells of, never ends below `flag_for_review` because of a setting, even with the responsible party handling it; `ongoing_harm_floor_applied` says when that held a result the setting would have lowered. Where the harm is discussed and not enacted (`fraud_report`, `abuse_report`, `support_disclosure`, `helpline`, `clinical`, `investigative`, `legal`, `advisory`, `training`, `journalism`, `research`, `moderation_review`) an urgent action is also capped to `flag_for_review`, and the response echoes `conversation_type_applied`. `direct_message`, `group_chat`, `public_post`, `customer_service` and `gaming_chat` change nothing. In `education` and `family` this applies only when the speaker is not the person at risk: a young person speaking for themselves to a teacher or a parent alerts as with no setting. Whenever a setting is in effect, from this field or from the account's `default_conversation_type`, the response names it in `conversation_type_in_effect` and says where it came from in `conversation_type_source`. When omitted here, the account-level `default_conversation_type` is used if one is set.

minor_disclosure_check.description: Optional, off unless true. For a platform that suspects users may get past its age verification. When true and the request declares an adult (an adult `age_group`, `child_age` of 18 or more, or `conversation_type` `dating`, `adult_community` or `workplace`), one extra narrow reading asks whether the speaker says they are under 18 in other words than a stated age (a school year, parental controls, a milestone), beside the analysis. On a yes the analysis runs without the declared age and adult audience, `declared_age_overridden` and `minor_disclosure` say so, and on `dating` or `adult_community` a result that asked for nothing is raised to `flag_for_review` (`minor_on_adult_platform_raised`). With it on, a plainly stated minor age ("im 15") is reported in `minor_disclosure` and raised on `dating` or `adult_community` the same way, with no extra call. Omitted or false: no extra call and behaviour is unchanged. A plainly stated minor age ("im 15") drops the declared adult age whatever this is set to, as it always has.

role.description: Role of the sender (e.g., "user", "contact", "adult", "child")

prior_messages.description: Prior turns of this conversation, oldest first, submitted by you for this request only -- Tuteliq stores no message content, so nothing here is retained after the call completes. Use this when you already have the whole conversation in hand; use continuation_token instead when you are calling once per new message as it arrives.

flag_profanity.description: Additive, deterministic word-list flag for plain profanity/vulgarity, applied to the bullying and unsafe results only. Adds `profanity` to those results; never affects detected/severity/risk_score/recommended_action. Free — no extra credits.

flag_risk_terms.description: Additive, deterministic word-list flag for bare drug and violence terms, applied to the bullying and unsafe results only. Adds `risk_terms` to those results; never affects detected/severity/risk_score/recommended_action. Purely lexical: WILL fire on benign uses of an included term ("kill the lights"). Free — no extra credits.

external_id.description: Your unique identifier (e.g. message ID, content ID) for correlating Tuteliq results with your own system. Echoed back in the response and included in webhook payloads so you can match alerts to the original content.

customer_id.description: Your end-customer identifier for multi-tenant / B2B2C scenarios. If you serve multiple customers (schools, apps, brands) from a single API key, set this to route webhook alerts to the correct customer. Echoed back in the response and included in webhook payloads as "customerId".

metadata.description: Arbitrary key-value pairs for additional context (e.g. { "channel": "discord", "region": "eu" }). Stored with the detection result, echoed in the response, and included in webhook payloads. Maximum 20 properties.

incident_moderation_enabled.description: Per-call override of your account incident logging setting. When set, it takes precedence for THIS request: true forces the incident to be persisted, false suppresses persistence. Omit to use your account default (which itself defaults to enabled). It is a provenance hint, not a cap -- always route on recommended_action, which can be anything up to immediate_intervention.

The code is the documented form; the English name of a supported language is also accepted ("English" as "en"). A region or script suffix is read as its base language ("en-US" as "en"), and "nb" or "nn" as "no". A value that is not supported is refused with a 400 that lists the supported codes. Omit the field, or send "auto", and the language is detected from the text.

conversation_type.description: Optional, no default: omit it and behaviour is unchanged. The setting this conversation was captured in, declared by your platform from its own configuration, never from end-user input. A declared setting names the responsible party in the conversation: a counsellor or helpline worker (`helpline`, `clinical`), a clinician (`healthcare`), an officer or investigator (`law_enforcement`, `investigative`), an adviser taking a report (`fraud_report`, `abuse_report`, `support_disclosure`, `advisory`), a moderator (`moderation_review`), a lawyer, trainer, journalist or researcher (`legal`, `training`, `journalism`, `research`), a teacher, tutor or safeguarding lead (`education`), a parent or guardian (`family`). In any of these settings, a conversation in which a person is at risk, that responsible party is already handling it, and nothing is happening as the text is written, is kept visible at `monitor` without an alert, and `protective_speech_capped` says so. Harm being done in the conversation, by anyone including the responsible party, a person at risk with nobody acting, and anything acute alert as they would with no setting. On social engineering, app fraud, romance scam, mule recruitment, gambling harm and bullying, harm happening now to the writer, or to a specific other person the writer tells of, never ends below `flag_for_review` because of a setting, even with the responsible party handling it; `ongoing_harm_floor_applied` says when that held a result the setting would have lowered. Where the harm is discussed and not enacted (`fraud_report`, `abuse_report`, `support_disclosure`, `helpline`, `clinical`, `investigative`, `legal`, `advisory`, `training`, `journalism`, `research`, `moderation_review`) an urgent action is also capped to `flag_for_review`, and the response echoes `conversation_type_applied`. `direct_message`, `group_chat`, `public_post`, `customer_service` and `gaming_chat` change nothing. In `education` and `family` this applies only when the speaker is not the person at risk: a young person speaking for themselves to a teacher or a parent alerts as with no setting. Whenever a setting is in effect, from this field or from the account's `default_conversation_type`, the response names it in `conversation_type_in_effect` and says where it came from in `conversation_type_source`. When omitted here, the account-level `default_conversation_type` is used if one is set.

minor_disclosure_check.description: Optional, off unless true. For a platform that suspects users may get past its age verification. When true and the request declares an adult (an adult `age_group`, `child_age` of 18 or more, or `conversation_type` `dating`, `adult_community` or `workplace`), one extra narrow reading asks whether the speaker says they are under 18 in other words than a stated age (a school year, parental controls, a milestone), beside the analysis. On a yes the analysis runs without the declared age and adult audience, `declared_age_overridden` and `minor_disclosure` say so, and on `dating` or `adult_community` a result that asked for nothing is raised to `flag_for_review` (`minor_on_adult_platform_raised`). With it on, a plainly stated minor age ("im 15") is reported in `minor_disclosure` and raised on `dating` or `adult_community` the same way, with no extra call. Omitted or false: no extra call and behaviour is unchanged. A plainly stated minor age ("im 15") drops the declared adult age whatever this is set to, as it always has.

delete.description: Cancels an active verification session. The mobile device will be notified via SSE. Refused while a submission is in progress: its verdict follows instead.

post.summary: Analyze a PDF or image for safety and compliance concerns
post.description: Upload a PDF (max 50MB, max 100 pages) or a single image (png, jpeg, webp) for multi-endpoint safety analysis. PDFs are read from the text layer per page; images are read by OCR and analysed as a one-page document. Choose which detectors run with the endpoints field. For a messaging screenshot, set split_by_sender=true to have the conversation split into messages with a side attributed to each, so the detector judges the last received message with the rest as history; this costs one additional vision call. Returns per-page results with an overall risk assessment, plus a SHA-256 hash of the uploaded file for chain-of-custody verification. Zero-retention: no document or image data is stored after processing.

document_hash.description: SHA-256 hash of the uploaded PDF for chain-of-custody verification

pages_analyzed.description: Pages with extractable text that were analyzed

text_layer_pages.description: Pages where text was extracted from the PDF text layer (always 0 for image uploads)

ocr_pages.description: Pages read by OCR — every page of an image upload, and PDF pages with no usable text layer

failed_pages.description: Pages with insufficient text for analysis

average_ocr_confidence.description: Average OCR confidence (0.0-1.0) across OCR pages

overall_risk_score.description: Highest risk score across all pages

incident_moderation_enabled.description: Per-call override of account incident logging: "true" forces persistence, "false" suppresses it. Omit for account default.

post.summary: Detect AI-generated or synthetic content
post.description: Analyzes text for AI-generated content indicators including LLM-generated text, synthetic identities, AI-enhanced grooming scripts, and synthetic CSAM. Classifies content as confirmed_synthetic, suspected_synthetic, unknown, or confirmed_authentic.

role.description: Who this participant is, as your platform knows it.

age_group.description: This participant's age group, for example "8-10". For a child or teen it gives the child's age the detectors use.

sender.description: The sender, as your platform knows them. Declared, like an age: never inferred from the text.

role.description: Who this participant is, as your platform knows it.

age_group.description: This participant's age group, for example "8-10". For a child or teen it gives the child's age the detectors use.

relationship_to_sender.description: How this recipient is related to the sender. `guardian_of_sender` or `child_of_sender` applies the `family` setting; `educator_of_sender` or `student_of_sender` applies `education`.

recipients.description: The recipients and how each is related to the sender. A declared relationship supplies the setting, and a declared child or teen supplies the child's age, where the request did not send them; `participants_applied` in the response says what was applied. It never excuses harm: a declared guardian or educator doing harm is flagged like anyone else.

language.description: Language code (e.g., "en"). 33 supported languages: en is stable, the other 32 are beta (ar, bg, ca, cs, da, de, el, es, et, fi, fr, ga, hr, hu, it, ja, ko, lt, lv, mt, nl, no, pl, pt, ro, ru, sk, sl, sv, tr, uk, zh). The code is the documented form; the English name of a supported language is also accepted ("English" as "en"). A region or script suffix is read as its base language ("en-US" as "en"), and "nb" or "nn" as "no". A value that is not supported is refused with a 400 that lists the supported codes. Omit the field, or send "auto", and the language is detected from the text.

conversation_type.description: Optional, no default: omit it and behaviour is unchanged. The setting this conversation was captured in, declared by your platform from its own configuration, never from end-user input. A declared setting names the responsible party in the conversation: a counsellor or helpline worker (`helpline`, `clinical`), a clinician (`healthcare`), an officer or investigator (`law_enforcement`, `investigative`), an adviser taking a report (`fraud_report`, `abuse_report`, `support_disclosure`, `advisory`), a moderator (`moderation_review`), a lawyer, trainer, journalist or researcher (`legal`, `training`, `journalism`, `research`), a teacher, tutor or safeguarding lead (`education`), a parent or guardian (`family`). In any of these settings, a conversation in which a person is at risk, that responsible party is already handling it, and nothing is happening as the text is written, is kept visible at `monitor` without an alert, and `protective_speech_capped` says so. Harm being done in the conversation, by anyone including the responsible party, a person at risk with nobody acting, and anything acute alert as they would with no setting. On social engineering, app fraud, romance scam, mule recruitment, gambling harm and bullying, harm happening now to the writer, or to a specific other person the writer tells of, never ends below `flag_for_review` because of a setting, even with the responsible party handling it; `ongoing_harm_floor_applied` says when that held a result the setting would have lowered. Where the harm is discussed and not enacted (`fraud_report`, `abuse_report`, `support_disclosure`, `helpline`, `clinical`, `investigative`, `legal`, `advisory`, `training`, `journalism`, `research`, `moderation_review`) an urgent action is also capped to `flag_for_review`, and the response echoes `conversation_type_applied`. `direct_message`, `group_chat`, `public_post`, `customer_service` and `gaming_chat` change nothing. In `education` and `family` this applies only when the speaker is not the person at risk: a young person speaking for themselves to a teacher or a parent alerts as with no setting. Whenever a setting is in effect, from this field or from the account's `default_conversation_type`, the response names it in `conversation_type_in_effect` and says where it came from in `conversation_type_source`.

minor_disclosure_check.description: Optional, off unless true. For a platform that suspects users may get past its age verification. When true and the request declares an adult (an adult `age_group`, `child_age` of 18 or more, or `conversation_type` `dating`, `adult_community` or `workplace`), one extra narrow reading asks whether the speaker says they are under 18 in other words than a stated age (a school year, parental controls, a milestone), beside the analysis. On a yes the analysis runs without the declared age and adult audience, `declared_age_overridden` and `minor_disclosure` say so, and on `dating` or `adult_community` a result that asked for nothing is raised to `flag_for_review` (`minor_on_adult_platform_raised`). With it on, a plainly stated minor age ("im 15") is reported in `minor_disclosure` and raised on `dating` or `adult_community` the same way, with no extra call. Omitted or false: no extra call and behaviour is unchanged. A plainly stated minor age ("im 15") drops the declared adult age whatever this is set to, as it always has.

age_group.description: Age group (e.g., "13-15")

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code (e.g., "GB", "US", "SE") for geo-localised helpline data. Falls back to user profile country if omitted.

include_evidence.description: Include evidence excerpts in response. Default: true.

support_threshold.description: Minimum severity level to include crisis support resources. Defaults to "high". Note: "critical" severity always includes support resources regardless of this setting.

verdict_only.description: Fast mode: omit the per-message `message_analysis` array from the response. All other fields are unchanged. Cuts output length (and therefore latency) significantly on multi-turn input.

support_threshold.description: Top-level alias for options.support_threshold. Minimum severity to show crisis support resources (default: high). Critical always shows.

include_evidence.description: Top-level alias for options.include_evidence. When false, the `evidence` array is omitted from the response. Default: true.

continuation_token.description: Opaque, signed token returned by a previous call to this endpoint. Pass it back here to continue the analysis with prior context — no need to re-send prior_messages. The token IS the state; we store nothing.

reset_conversation.description: When true, discard any continuation_token and treat this call as the first turn of a new conversation.

message_id.description: Optional customer-side identifier for this turn. If provided, evidence pointers in the continuation_token will reference this id so you can map detections back to your own messages. If omitted we use a deterministic short hash of the text.

bypass_cache.description: Deprecated, no effect: results are never cached — every request runs a fresh evaluation and nothing derived from the input is stored. The field is still accepted so existing integrations do not break.

external_id.description: Your unique identifier (e.g. message ID, content ID) for correlating Tuteliq results with your own system. Echoed back in the response and included in webhook payloads so you can match alerts to the original content.

customer_id.description: Your end-customer identifier for multi-tenant / B2B2C scenarios. If you serve multiple customers (schools, apps, brands) from a single API key, set this to route webhook alerts to the correct customer. Echoed back in the response and included in webhook payloads as "customerId".

metadata.description: Arbitrary key-value pairs for additional context (e.g. { "channel": "discord", "region": "eu" }). Stored with the detection result, echoed in the response, and included in webhook payloads. Maximum 20 properties.

incident_moderation_enabled.description: Per-call override of your account incident logging setting. When set, it takes precedence for THIS request: true forces the incident to be persisted, false suppresses persistence. Omit to use your account default (which itself defaults to enabled). Useful to suppress logging for test traffic or to opt specific calls in or out.

declared_age_overridden.description: True when the caller declared an adult age group but the speaker states a minor age in the message or in the earlier turns sent with it. The declared age was not used. Nothing is escalated by this on its own; the analysis runs as if no age had been sent. Worth investigating at your end: an age check that disagrees with what the user says is what a bypassed age verification looks like. A stated ADULT age never has this effect. Absent unless it applied.

declared_age_overridden_reason.description: Human-readable explanation. Present only when declared_age_overridden is true.

minor_disclosure.description: Present when the request declared an adult and the speaker says they are under 18, by stating an age or in other words. The declared adult age or setting was then not used, and `declared_age_overridden` says so. Never set by a stated adult age. Absent otherwise.

detected.description: Always true when the object is present.

message_index.description: 0-based index into the turns read (earlier turns first, the message last; for grooming, `messages`).

suggested_age_group.description: The value to send back as `context.age_group` on this user's later requests. Tuteliq stores nothing: your platform carries the signal forward. Always a minor band, never an adult value: `under 18` by default, or `under 13`, `13-15` or `16-17` when the speaker stated an age. Sent back, it is read as a minor age group, so a minor's protections apply, and with `conversation_type` `dating`, `adult_community` or `workplace` the declared child beats the setting: the adult audience is not used.

{"disabled_endpoints": ["grooming", "bullying"]}

The override is persisted to the incident document and a separate signed Art 12 audit receipt is emitted linking back to the original. The optional reason_comment is encrypted with the customer's registered public key (end-to-end) when enabled; otherwise server-side AES.

post.summary: Submit the same moderator review across multiple incidents (Art 14, bulk)
post.description: Applies the same review action + reason to up to 100 incidents in one call. Each incident emits its own signed Art 12 audit receipt — bulk is a UX shortcut, not a compliance shortcut. Per-incident success/error is returned so a partial failure can be retried without re-running successful items.

get.summary: DSA transparency report data for a reporting period
get.description: Aggregated moderation data from your account to help prepare a transparency report on the template of Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2835. Every template indicator is listed with its availability: computed from your Tuteliq records, partial (Tuteliq holds part of what the indicator needs, and `reason` says what is missing), or not_held_by_tuteliq (your platform supplies it; the value is always null). Detections are grouped under the template's content categories through a published mapping (`category_mapping`); detections with no single template category are listed in `unmapped_categories` for you to classify. Test traffic is excluded. No incident content is read or returned. Reads at most 100,000 incidents per request. Included in the Build, Assure and Enterprise plans on an active subscription; not in legacy plans, free plans or trials. Cost: 1 credit per started block of 10,000 incidents read in the period, test incidents included (1 credit up to 10,000, 2 up to 20,000, 10 at 100,000; never less than 1). The JSON response reports the count read in scope.incidents_scanned and the charge in credits_used.

parameters.description: First day of the reporting period, YYYY-MM-DD (UTC), included.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Last day of the reporting period, YYYY-MM-DD (UTC), included. At most 366 days after `from`.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: json (default), or csv: one RFC 4180 row per template indicator and per category metric, UTF-8.

post.summary: Report a device attestation (endpoint agent check-in)
post.description: The tuteliq-agent CLI evaluates the org's device-safety policy locally and reports the pass/fail result here. One latest-state record is kept per device (upsert, no history). The org is derived from the authenticated API key — any org_id in the body is ignored. No user content is stored; only device posture (policy rule results, versions, platform).

policy_id.description: Identifier of the evaluated policy manifest.

passed.description: True iff every policy rule passed.

rule.description: The evaluated policy rule (posture check — process/file/version/OS). Never contains user content.

detail.description: Human-readable reason the rule failed (omitted on pass).

attested_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the local evaluation.

org_id.description: Ignored — the org is always derived from the API key. Never trusted from the body.

expires_at.description: ISO 8601 expiry (attested_at + 90 days); Firestore TTL reaps the row after this.

get.summary: List the org's device fleet with a compliance summary
get.description: Returns every device's latest attestation for the caller's org (newest first) plus a rollup summary (total / compliant / non-compliant / compliance %). Read-only, deterministic, no LLM. Scoped to the API key's org.

get.summary: Get a single device's latest attestation
get.description: Returns the latest attestation for one device in the caller's org. 404 if the device has never checked in (or belongs to another org).
